arxiv-2104-01442.title: Cell cycle length and long-time behaviour of an age-size model
arxiv-2104-01442.creator: Katarzyna Pichór, Ryszard Rudnicki
arxiv-2104-01442.description: Abstract . We consider an age-size structured cell population model based on the cell cycle length. The model is described by a first order partial differential equation with initial-boundary conditions. Using the theory of semigroups of positive operators we establish new criteria for an asynchronous exponential growth of solutions to such equations.

arxiv-2204-04910.title: A-DRIVE: Autonomous Deadlock Detection and Recovery at Road Intersections for Connected and Automated Vehicles
arxiv-2204-04910.creator: Shunsuke Aoki 1 , Ragunathan (Raj) Rajkumar 2
arxiv-2204-04910.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shunsuke Aoki 1 , Ragunathan (Raj) Rajkumar 2. Connected and Automated Vehicles (CAVs) are highly expected to improve traffic throughput and safety at road intersections, single-track lanes, and construction zones. However, multiple CAVs can block each other and create a mutual deadlock around these road segments (i) when vehicle systems have a failure, such as a communication failure, control failure, or localization failure and/or (ii) when vehicles use a long shared road segment.

arxiv-2307-11455.title: Spectropolarimetry of Type II supernovae
arxiv-2307-11455.creator: T. Nagao, , S. Mattila, R. Kotak, H. Kuncarayakti
arxiv-2307-11455.description: Abstract We investigate polarization spectra of hydrogen-rich core-collapse supernovae (Type II SNe). The polarization signal from SNe contains two independent components: intrinsic SN polarization and interstellar polarization (ISP). From these components, we can study the SN explosion geometry and the dust properties in their host galaxies or in the Milky Way.

arxiv-2407-06092.title: Assessing Cardiomegaly in Dogs Using a Simple CNN Model
arxiv-2407-06092.creator: Nikhil Deekonda
arxiv-2407-06092.description: Abstract This paper introduces DogHeart [ 4 ] , a dataset comprising 1400 training, 200 validation, and 400 test images categorized as small, normal, and large based on VHS score. A custom CNN model is developed, featuring a straightforward architecture with 4 convolutional layers and 4 fully connected layers.

arxiv-2411-10494.title: Efficient inference for differential equation models without numerical solvers
arxiv-2411-10494.creator: Alexander Johnston, Ruth E. Baker, Matthew J. Simpson
arxiv-2411-10494.description: Abstract Parameter inference is essential when interpreting observational data using mathematical models. Standard inference methods for differential equation models typically rely on obtaining repeated numerical solutions of the differential equation(s). Recent results have explored how numerical truncation error can have major, detrimental, and sometimes hidden impacts on likelihood-based inference by introducing false local maxima into the log-likelihood function.

arxiv-2507-08594.title: Generating Proto-Personas through Prompt Engineering: A Case Study on Efficiency, Effectiveness and Empathy DOI: 10.XXXX/0000000.0000000 Conference: XXXVIII Brazilian Symposium on Software Engineering; October, 2025; PE XXXVIII Brazilian Symposium on Software Engineering (SBES 2025), October, 2025,
arxiv-2507-08594.creator: Fernando Ayach, Vitor Lameirão, Raul Leão, Jerfferson Felizardo, Rafael Sobrinho, Vanessa Borges, Patrícia Matsubara, Awdren Fontão
arxiv-2507-08594.description: Abstract . Proto-personas are commonly used during early-stage Product Discovery, such as Lean Inception, to guide product definition and stakeholder alignment. However, the manual creation of proto-personas is often time-consuming, cognitively demanding, and prone to bias. In this paper, we propose and empirically investigate a prompt engineering-based approach to generate proto-personas with the support of Generative AI (GenAI).

arxiv-2508-02528.title: From Pixels to Pathology: Restoration Diffusion for Diagnostic-Consistent Virtual IHC
arxiv-2508-02528.creator: Jingsong Liu, Xiaofeng Deng, Han Li, Azar Kazemi, Christian Grashei, Gesa Wilkens, Xin You, Tanja Groll, Nassir Navab, Carolin Mogler, Peter J. Schüffler
arxiv-2508-02528.description: Abstract Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining is the clinical standard for assessing tissue morphology, but it lacks molecular-level diagnostic information. In contrast, immunohistochemistry (IHC) provides crucial insights into biomarker expression, such as HER2 status for breast cancer grading, but remains costly and time-consuming, limiting its use in time-sensitive clinical workflows.

arxiv-2509-23861.title: Investigating Multi-layer Representations for Dense Passage Retrieval
arxiv-2509-23861.creator: Zhongbin Xie, Thomas Lukasiewicz
arxiv-2509-23861.description: Abstract Dense retrieval models usually adopt vectors from the last hidden layer of the document encoder to represent a document, which is in contrast to the fact that representations in different layers of a pre-trained language model usually contain different kinds of linguistic knowledge, and behave differently during fine-tuning.

arxiv-2602-19572.title: Extracting Patterns of Chemical Information from Differential Mobility Spectrometry Measurements under Varying Conditions of Humidity and Temperature
arxiv-2602-19572.creator: Philipp Müller 1∗ , Gary A. Eiceman 2 , Anton Rauhameri 1 , Anton Kontunen 1,3 , Antti Roine 1,3 , Niku Oksala 1,3,4 , Antti Vehkaoja 1 , and Maiju Lepomäki 1,5
arxiv-2602-19572.description: Abstract . Differential Mobility Spectrometry (DMS), also known as Field Asymmetric Ion Mobility Spectrometry, is a rapid and affordable technology for extracting information from gas phase samples containing complex volatile organic compounds, and can therefore be used for analyzing surgical smoke.

europmc-pmc5796205.creator: Luo J, Zhou JJ, Zhang JZ.
europmc-pmc5796205.description: Auxin plays a crucial role in the diverse cellular and developmental responses of plants across their lifespan. pmc-10607784.title: Biosecurity and Management Strategies for Economically Important Exotic Tephritid Fruit Fly Species in Australia
pmc-10607784.creator: Jessica L Hoskins, Polychronis Rempoulakis, Mark M Stevens, Bernard C Dominiak, Xingeng Wang
pmc-10607784.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Simple SummaryAustralian horticulture is at risk from incursions by exotic tephritid fruit fly species, particularly oriental fruit fly. An incursion by exotic fruit flies is likely to result in global trade restrictions and will cause significant economic losses. In this study, we investigated global management strategies for exotic fruit fly species and compared them with available local strategies in Australia to identify areas where Australian management practices could be improved.

pmc-10611310.title: Wrist-Worn Sensor Validation for Heart Rate Variability and Electrodermal Activity Detection in a Stressful Driving Environment
pmc-10611310.creator: Simone Costantini, Mattia Chiappini, Giorgia Malerba, Carla Dei, Anna Falivene, Sara Arlati, Vera Colombo, Emilia Biffi, Fabio Alexander Storm, Ki H Chon
pmc-10611310.description: Wearable sensors are widely used to gather psychophysiological data in the laboratory and real-world applications. However, the accuracy of these devices should be carefully assessed. The study focused on testing the accuracy of the Empatica 4 (E4) wristband for the detection of heart rate variability (HRV) and electrodermal activity (EDA) metrics in stress-inducing conditions and growing-risk driving scenarios.

pmc-10624840.title: Brain activity characteristics of RGB stimulus: an EEG study
pmc-10624840.creator: Alireza Khadir, Mohammad Maghareh, Shamim Sasani Ghamsari, Borhan Beigzadeh
pmc-10624840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The perception of color is a fundamental cognitive feature of our psychological experience, with an essential role in many aspects of human behavior. Several studies used magnetoencephalography, functional magnetic resonance imaging, and electroencephalography (EEG) approaches to investigate color perception. Their methods includes the event-related potential and spectral power activity of different color spaces, such as Derrington-Krauskopf-Lennie and red-green-blue (RGB), in addition to exploring the psychological and emotional effects of colors.

pmc-11516030.title: The German Status Report on Climate Change and Health 2023
pmc-11516030.creator: K Kelleher, M Mlinaric, H Niemann, T Ziese
pmc-11516030.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The German Status Report on Climate Change and Health was coordinated by the Robert Koch Institute, Germany’s public health institute, and published in 2023 through a collaboration of approximately 100 authors from 30 German institutions.

pmc-11642193.title: Factors Associated with the Severity of ERCP-Related Complications: A Retrospective Single-Centre Study
pmc-11642193.creator: Kristel Goubert, Helena Degroote, Martine De Vos, Maxim Khalenkow, Pieter Hindryckx, László Czakõ
pmc-11642193.description: Objectives: Risk factors for post-endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) complications have been extensively studied and are well established; most complications are mild and self-limiting. This study aims to identify patients at risk of severe early post-ERCP complications. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study with data from 2810 ERCP procedures performed at Ghent University Hospital between 2016 and 2022.

pmc-12379344.title: Mental health rehabilitation models for people with complex psychosis: a systematic review
pmc-12379344.creator: Nikola Houngbedji, Christian Dalton-Locke, Amelia Hughes, Helen Killaspy
pmc-12379344.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMental health rehabilitation services support people with complex psychosis to live successfully in the community. This systematic review aimed to identify and compare the approach and effectiveness of different models of mental health rehabilitation.MethodsSix online databases (PsycINFO, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, CINAHL Plus, MEDLINE and Emcare) were searched for quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies published since 2000 that described mental health rehabilitation models. The search was extended by screening references and citations of included studies.

pmc-12445768.title: Stopping versus continuing renin-angiotensin system inhibitors before surgery: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
pmc-12445768.creator: Marwah Algodi, Omar Saab, Alhareth Al-Sagban, Hashim T. Hashim, Ahmed D. Al-Obaidi, Mohanad Albayyaa, Bashar Al-Hemyari
pmc-12445768.description: Background and Aims:The optimal perioperative management of patients chronically using renin-angiotensin system inhibitors (RASIs) is still uncertain. This study aims to compare the outcomes of withholding versus continuing RASIs before surgery, focusing on efficacy and safety.Methods:A systematic review and meta-analysis synthesising evidence from randomised controlled trials (RCTs) obtained from PubMed, CENTRAL, Scopus, and Web of Science until September 2024.

pmc-12659051.title: Integration of multi-omics data and phenotyping provides insights into purple leaf sheaths color in millet seedling stage
pmc-12659051.creator: Min Zhang, Yu Zhao, Jiujun Du, Jihan Cui, Meihong Huang, Jingxin Wang, Lijuan Zhao, Fengyan Cao, Cheng Chu, Shunguo Li, Xueyan Xia
pmc-12659051.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundThe millet, an important coarse grain crop, exhibits drought resistance, water conservation efficiency, and adaptability to poor soil conditions. Although the purple leaf sheath is a prevalent phenotype, the underlying mechanisms of color variation remain unclear. Previous studies suggested that leaf sheath coloration might result from differential accumulation of plant pigments, yet the key substances and molecular mechanisms governing color formation in millet have not been systematically elucidated.ResultsWe investigated the metabolic pathway underlying millet leaf sheath coloration using multi-omics analysis.

pmc-12730497.title: Modulation of BDNF/TrkB Signalling Pathway in Alzheimer’s Disease: Mechanistic Insights and the Role of Stem Cell Therapy
pmc-12730497.creator: Zairin Zulaikha Harun, Auji Abdul Azhar, Yun-Jin Kim, Farah Wahida Ibrahim, Min-Hwei Ng, Jen-Kit Tan, Yogeswaran Lokanathan
pmc-12730497.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease, characterized by the accumulation of amyloid beta (aβ) plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, along with progressive deterioration of cognitive function. AD is the most common form of dementia and affects over 55 million people worldwide. Current treatments for AD are symptomatic-based rather than curative, which calls for the development of new therapeutic strategies.

pmc-13349218.title: Breaking the Size Barrier: Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection of a Massive Flat Gastric Neuroendocrine Tumor
pmc-13349218.creator: Gennaro Tagliamonte, Mariangela Giunta, Davide Ravizza, Eleonora Pisa, Giuseppe De Roberto
pmc-13349218.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Type I gastric neuroendocrine tumors, arising in chronic atrophic gastritis, are usually small, mucosal, or submucosal elevated lesions. Current guidelines recommend endoscopic resection of lesions ≤20 mm and surgical treatment for those >20 mm. We report an unusual case of a 56-year-old woman with a completely flat (Paris 0-IIb) gastric body neuroendocrine tumor (NET) measuring 140 × 35 mm, detected by virtual chromoendoscopy and successfully resected by endoscopic submucosal dissection without complications. Histology revealed about 40 well-differentiated low-grade NET foci.

pmc-13399307.title: Assessing the microstructure of simple rhamphothecae in chickens (Aves: Galliformes: Gallus gallus domesticus)
pmc-13399307.creator: Khanh H. T. To, Michelle R. Stocker, Tobin L. Hieronymus
pmc-13399307.description: Corneous sheaths on the jaws of beaked tetrapods, or rhamphothecae, are classified as simple or compound based on their external morphology. In birds, simple rhamphothecae possess single corneous sheaths covering the upper jaws and the mandibles, respectively, rather than the several corneous plates of compound rhamphothecae.
